rv.q: The ending is gripping in the most heartbreaking way, as Councell does a beautiful job capturing the pain, disappointment, and inner turmoil...
The spare intimacy of the small studio space at the Greenhouse Theater Center and the performances mostly work at drawing us in.
Smartly directed by Enrico Spada , Year One uses historical events as an allegory for our current political climate.
The cast of five is quite capable with strong performances by Pavlovich and Copeland as the young couple.
There are canyon-sized cracks in Gernand’s belief that Year One is a villain-less play.
There’s a wishy-washiness to “Year One” that saps its impact.
